## Purpose

This SOP describes standardized procedures for decontaminating field
equipment between sampling sites and between field outings. Proper
decontamination serves two purposes: (1) preventing cross-contamination
of samples that would compromise analytical results, and (2) preventing
the transfer of invasive species, pathogens, and nuisance organisms
between water bodies and field sites [@cdfw_ais2016; @hosea2005].
These procedures apply to all equipment that contacts environmental
media (water, soil, sediment, biological tissue) or that is transported
between sites.


## Scope

- **Applies to:** All reusable field sampling equipment, wading gear
  (boots, waders, nets), sampling instruments (sondes, meters),
  containers, and hand tools used at EA Program field sites
- **Does not apply to:** Disposable, single-use items (e.g.,
  individually packaged sterile Colilert bottles, disposable filter
  cartridges); laboratory glassware cleaning (see
  [SOP-L101](../lab_sops/SOP-L101-glassware-cleaning.qmd)); drone or
  camera equipment (wipe with dry cloth only unless visibly
  contaminated)
- **Location:** Performed at field sites (between-site decontamination)
  and in the lab (post-field cleaning in SGM 131--134)


## Responsibilities

| Role              | Responsibility                                          |
|:------------------|:--------------------------------------------------------|
| PI / Field Lead   | Ensure decontamination supplies are on the equipment checklist; verify compliance |
| Trained Personnel | Decontaminate equipment per this SOP before and after each site visit |
| New Students      | Complete training before independent fieldwork          |


## Definitions

- **2% bleach solution:** A dilute sodium hypochlorite solution prepared
  by adding 200 mL of household bleach (5--8% NaOCl) to 10 L of tap
  water; the standard decontamination solution for wading gear, nets,
  and hand tools in the EA Program; must be prepared fresh each field
  day as bleach degrades within hours [@cdfw_ais2016].
- **Aquatic invasive species (AIS):** Non-native organisms introduced
  to a water body where they cause ecological or economic harm; common
  AIS of concern in Southern California include New Zealand mudsnail,
  quagga mussel, didymo, and chytrid fungus; transferred between
  water bodies on wet gear [@cdfw_ais2016].
- **Chytrid fungus (*Batrachochytrium dendrobatidis*, Bd):** A
  waterborne pathogenic fungus lethal to many amphibian species;
  transmitted via contaminated water, soil, and equipment; killed by
  2% bleach or thermal decontamination at 60 °C [@hosea2005].
- **Cross-contamination:** Transfer of analytes, biological material,
  or organisms from one sample or site to another via inadequately
  cleaned equipment; can invalidate analytical results and introduce
  invasive species.
- **Didymo (*Didymosphenia geminata*):** A freshwater diatom that forms
  dense mats on stream substrates; tolerates damp conditions for many
  hours; felt-soled wading boots are a primary vector; killed by
  2% bleach or drying for at least 48 hours [@cdfw_ais2016].
- **Equipment blank:** A sample of deionized water rinsed through
  decontaminated sampling equipment and collected as a QC sample;
  analyzed alongside field samples to verify that decontamination
  removes analytes below detection limits.
- **New Zealand mudsnail (*Potamopyrgus antipodarum*):** An invasive
  snail less than 5 mm long that survives transit on damp wading gear
  for up to 28 hours; a significant concern in Southern California
  streams; killed by 2% bleach immersion for at least 10 minutes or
  thermal decontamination at 60 °C [@hosea2005].
- **Thermal decontamination:** Application of water at ≥ 60 °C to kill
  aquatic invasive species and pathogens; preferred over bleach for
  equipment sensitive to sodium hypochlorite (rubber gaskets, sensor
  membranes) [@hosea2005; @cdfw_ais2016].


## Safety and Hazards

::: {.callout-warning}
### Hazards

- **Chemical:** Dilute bleach (sodium hypochlorite) is a skin and eye
  irritant and can damage clothing. Handle with gloves and avoid
  splashing.
- **Physical:** Hot water (60 °C or above) used for thermal
  decontamination poses a scald risk. Use insulated containers and
  pour carefully.
- **Biological:** Equipment that has contacted contaminated water or
  soil may carry pathogens. Wear gloves during decontamination.
:::

### Required PPE

- [ ] Nitrile gloves
- [ ] Safety glasses (when using bleach solution)
- [ ] Lab coat or field clothing you are willing to bleach-stain

### Emergency Procedures

For bleach splashes to skin or eyes, flush with clean water for at
least 15 minutes. Refer to [SOP-F001 Field Safety](SOP-F001-field-safety.qmd)
and [SOP-L003 Hazardous Materials
Handling](../lab_sops/SOP-L003-hazardous-materials-handling.qmd).


## Equipment and Materials

### Decontamination Supplies

| Item                                      | Notes                               |
|:------------------------------------------|:------------------------------------|
| Household bleach (sodium hypochlorite, 5--8%) | For preparing 2% decon solution |
| Spray bottle (labeled "Decon -- Bleach 2%") | For applying solution in the field |
| Stiff-bristle scrub brush                 | For removing visible debris         |
| Bucket (5-gallon, dedicated)              | For soaking equipment               |
| Deionized or distilled water              | For final rinse of sampling equipment |
| Tap water (carboy or jug)                 | For initial rinse in the field      |
| Paper towels or clean rags                | For drying                          |
| Garbage bags                              | For isolating contaminated gear during transport |

### Solution Preparation

Prepare a **2% bleach solution** by adding 200 mL of household bleach
(5--8% sodium hypochlorite) to 10 L of tap water. Prepare fresh
solution each field day; bleach degrades within hours
[@cdfw_ais2016].

For **thermal decontamination** (alternative to bleach), heat water to
at least 60 °C. Preferred for equipment that may be damaged by bleach
(e.g., rubber gaskets, certain sensor membranes) [@hosea2005].


## Procedure

### Between-Site Decontamination (Field)

Perform the following steps before moving to the next sampling site.

**Wading gear (boots, waders, chest packs):**

1. Remove from the water body and inspect for visible organisms
   (snails, plant fragments, mud).
2. Use the scrub brush and tap water to remove all visible debris,
   paying special attention to boot soles, lace eyelets, and wader
   seams.
3. Spray all surfaces with 2% bleach solution or immerse boot soles in
   the bleach bucket for at least one minute [@cdfw_ais2016].
4. Rinse with tap water to remove bleach residue before entering the
   next water body.

**Nets, sieves, and kick screens:**

1. Remove all visible organisms and debris by hand and with the scrub
   brush.
2. Soak in 2% bleach solution for at least one minute, or pour hot
   water (≥ 60 °C) over all mesh surfaces [@hosea2005].
3. Rinse with tap water.

**Sampling instruments (sondes, meters, tubing):**

1. Rinse the sensor housing and cable with tap water.
2. Wipe external surfaces with a cloth dampened with DI water.
3. Do not immerse sensitive electronics in bleach. If the manufacturer
   recommends a specific decontamination procedure, follow it instead.

**Hand tools (trowels, augers, calipers, measuring tapes):**

1. Scrub off visible soil or sediment with tap water and the brush.
2. Spray with 2% bleach solution or rinse with DI water.
3. Dry with paper towels before packing.

### Post-Field Decontamination (Laboratory)

Upon return to the lab, before storing equipment:

1. Unpack all field equipment in the designated cleaning area (SGM 134
   sink or outdoor wash area).
2. Repeat the cleaning steps from §6.1, using DI water for the final
   rinse of any equipment that contacts samples.
3. Allow all equipment to air-dry completely before storing.
   Incompletely dried equipment promotes mold and bacterial growth.
4. Inspect nets and mesh for tears; report damage to the lab manager.
5. Return all equipment to designated storage locations per
   [SOP-L007](../lab_sops/SOP-L007-equipment-inventory.qmd).

### Invasive Species of Concern

The following organisms are of particular concern in Southern California
watersheds [@cdfw_ais2016; @hosea2005]:

| Organism | Concern |
|:----------------------------------|:------------------------------------|
| New Zealand mudsnail (*Potamopyrgus antipodarum*) | < 5 mm; survives on wet gear up to 28 hours |
| Quagga/zebra mussel (*Dreissena* spp.) | Veligers invisible to the naked eye |
| Didymo (*Didymosphenia geminata*) | Algal cells survive on damp felt soles |
| Chytrid fungus (*Batrachochytrium dendrobatidis*) | Lethal to amphibians; transmitted via water and mud |
| Invasive aquatic plants (e.g., *Arundo donax* fragments) | Fragments root easily at new sites |

::: {.callout-important}
If sampling in a watershed known to harbor New Zealand mudsnails or
quagga mussels, use thermal decontamination (≥ 60 °C) rather than
bleach, as hot water is more reliably lethal to these organisms
[@hosea2005]. Allow gear to dry completely (at least 48 hours) before
using it at another site.
:::


## Quality Control

- The field lead verifies that decontamination supplies are packed
  before departure (include on the
  [SOP-F002 Field Equipment Checklist](SOP-F002-field-equipment-checklist.qmd)).
- At the start of each semester, inspect decontamination supplies
  (bleach expiration, brush condition, spray bottle function) and
  replace as needed.
- For chemical sampling, submit one equipment blank per sampling event:
  rinse decontaminated equipment with DI water and collect the rinse as
  a sample. Analyze alongside field samples to verify that
  decontamination removes analytes below detection limits.

## Training Record

Before performing field decontamination independently, personnel must:

1. Read this SOP in full
2. Demonstrate proper preparation of 2% bleach solution
3. Demonstrate between-site decontamination of wading gear and sampling
   equipment during a supervised field visit
4. Be signed off by the PI or field lead
